notes.DEU: 2011 年福島事故後決定廢核，最後 3 部機組 2023-04-15 停機（原訂 2022 年底）。
notes.ITA: 1987 年公投後關閉 4 座核電廠，最後一座 1990 年停機，2011 年公投再否決重建。2025 年 2 月政府通過重新開放核電的法案，2026 年 9 月國會通過（維基，2026-10-19 版）。
notes.LTU: 加入歐盟的條件：跟車諾比同型的伊格納利納核電廠 2009-12-31 關閉。
notes.ESP: 2023 年 12 月政府確認 2027–2035 年依序關閉 7 部機組；2025 年 4 月表示會考慮業者延長運轉的申請。
notes.CHE: 2011 年決定不延長運轉、不建新廠，2017 年起法律禁止新建核電廠。2026-06-18 國會通過取消禁令，2026 年 9 月反對者連署成功，要交付公投；公投前禁令仍有效。
notes.AUT: 1978 年公投否決啟用已蓋好的茨文滕多夫核電廠，同年立法禁止核電；1999 年再以憲法層級的法律禁止。
notes.AUS: 聯邦法律（1998 年的輻射防護與核子安全法、1999 年的環境保護與生物多樣性保育法）禁止興建核電廠。
notes.DNK: 1985 年國會決議禁止興建核電廠（是國會決議，不是法律）；2025 年政府開始評估取消。
notes.IRL: 1999 年的電力管制法禁止核能發電。
notes.URY: 1997 年第 16.832 號法律第 27 條禁止在國內使用核能（IMPO 法規資料庫的現行條文）。
notes.SRB: 1989 年起法律禁止核電，2024 年 11 月廢止。
notes.PRK: 寧邊的 5 MW 反應爐主要生產核武用的鈽，不算商用核電（GEM 列為運轉中）。
notes.PAN: 1968–1976 年巴拿馬運河區有一艘美國陸軍的核電船（GEM 列為退役）。
notes.PRI: 1960 年代有一座示範用的反應爐（GEM 列為退役）。
notes.HRV: 跟斯洛維尼亞共有克爾什科核電廠（在斯洛維尼亞）。
notes.NZL: 1987 年的無核區法禁止核武與核動力船，沒有禁止核電。
notes.BEL: 2003 年的廢核法 2025-05-17 廢止，不再廢核。
notes.KOR: 文在寅政府 2017 年的廢核政策 2022 年取消。
notes.SWE: 1980 年公投後的廢核政策 2009 年結束，2023 年政府宣布要蓋新的反應爐。
notes.NLD: 1994 年國會決議廢核，2005 年推翻；計畫新建 2 部機組。
notes.JPN: 2011 年福島事故後一度全部停機，2023 年內閣核准新建與延長運轉到 60 年。GEM 的興建中有大間、島根 3 號機，也有柏崎刈羽 7 號、東海第二、泊 3 號這些停機後的安全工程。
notes.USA: GEM 的興建中是帕利塞茲重新運轉、凱默勒（Natrium）、Hermes 測試爐與 Pele 軍用微型反應爐。
notes.UKR: 札波羅熱核電廠 6 部 2022 年起被俄軍占領、停機（GEM 仍列運轉中）；赫梅利尼茨基 3、4 號機 GEM 列為擱置。
notes.KAZ: 1999 年關閉阿克套唯一的核電廠（BN-350）；2024 年公投同意興建，2026 年政府核准至少 3 座新廠（維基）。
notes.PHL: 巴丹核電廠 1984 年蓋好但沒有運轉；2024 年請韓國水力原子力評估重新啟用。
notes.VNM: 2016 年放棄寧順核電計畫，2024 年 11 月國會核准恢復。
notes.HKG: 從廣東的大亞灣核電廠買電。
notes.TWN: 台灣 2025-05-17 核三廠 2 號機停機後沒有運轉中的核電機組（核一 2019、核二 2023 年停機），歸「已廢核」。2025-08-23 核三重新運轉的公投，同意票占有效票 74.2%，但只有選舉人的 21.7%，未達 25% 門檻不通過。2026 年 3 月賴清德總統宣布重啟核三、核二，台電 3 月 27 日向核安會提出核三再運轉計畫（目標 2028 年，核二 2029 年）；核安會 2026-08-31 表示審查總結會議後台電已繳交修訂版，計畫核定後還要完成自主安全檢查、換發運轉執照。2026-11-28 另有「廢除非核家園」的全國性公投（第 22 案）。

notesEn.DEU: Decided to phase out nuclear power after Fukushima in 2011; the last three units shut down on 15 April 2023 (originally planned for the end of 2022).
notesEn.ITA: Closed its four nuclear plants after a 1987 referendum, the last in 1990; a 2011 referendum rejected a revival. The government approved a bill to lift the ban on new nuclear power in February 2025, which Parliament passed in September 2026 (Wikipedia, 19 October 2026 revision).
notesEn.LTU: As a condition of joining the EU, the Ignalina plant (the same design as Chernobyl) closed on 31 December 2009.
notesEn.ESP: In December 2023 the government confirmed closing its seven reactors between 2027 and 2035; in April 2025 it said it would consider operators' requests to extend them.
notesEn.CHE: Decided in 2011 not to extend reactor lifetimes or build new ones; new nuclear plants have been banned by law since 2017. Parliament voted to lift the ban on 18 June 2026, but opponents forced a referendum in September 2026, and the ban stays until the vote.
notesEn.AUT: A 1978 referendum stopped the finished Zwentendorf plant from starting up, and a law banned nuclear power the same year; a constitutional law reaffirmed the ban in 1999.
notesEn.AUS: Federal law (the 1998 radiation protection and nuclear safety act and the 1999 environment protection and biodiversity conservation act) prohibits nuclear power plants.
notesEn.DNK: A 1985 parliamentary resolution bans building nuclear power plants (a resolution rather than a law); in 2025 the government began considering lifting it.
notesEn.IRL: The 1999 Electricity Regulation Act prohibits nuclear power generation.
notesEn.URY: Article 27 of Law 16.832 (1997) prohibits the use of nuclear energy in the country (current text in the IMPO legal database).
notesEn.SRB: Nuclear power was banned by law from 1989 until the law was repealed in November 2024.
notesEn.PRK: The 5 MW reactor at Yongbyon mainly produces plutonium for weapons and is not counted as commercial nuclear power (GEM lists it as operating).
notesEn.PAN: A US Army floating nuclear plant served the Panama Canal Zone from 1968 to 1976 (retired in GEM).
notesEn.PRI: Had a demonstration reactor in the 1960s (retired in GEM).
notesEn.HRV: Co-owns the Krško nuclear plant with Slovenia (located in Slovenia).
notesEn.NZL: The 1987 nuclear-free zone act bans nuclear weapons and nuclear-powered ships, not nuclear power.
notesEn.BEL: The 2003 phase-out law was repealed on 17 May 2025, ending the phase-out.
notesEn.KOR: The phase-out policy adopted by the Moon Jae-in government in 2017 was reversed in 2022.
notesEn.SWE: The phase-out policy that followed a 1980 referendum ended in 2009; in 2023 the government announced plans for new reactors.
notesEn.NLD: Parliament voted for a phase-out in 1994 and reversed it in 2005; two new units are planned.
notesEn.JPN: All reactors were shut down after Fukushima in 2011; in 2023 the cabinet approved new reactors and extending operation to 60 years. GEM's units under construction include Ohma and Shimane 3, as well as safety upgrades at idle units such as Kashiwazaki-Kariwa 7, Tokai 2 and Tomari 3.
notesEn.USA: GEM's units under construction are the Palisades restart, Kemmerer (Natrium), the Hermes test reactor and the Project Pele military microreactor.
notesEn.UKR: Zaporizhzhia's six units have been occupied by Russia and shut down since 2022 (still operating in GEM); GEM lists Khmelnytskyi 3 and 4 as shelved.
notesEn.KAZ: Closed its only plant (BN-350 at Aktau) in 1999; a 2024 referendum backed new construction, and in 2026 the government approved at least three new plants (Wikipedia).
notesEn.PHL: The Bataan plant was finished in 1984 but never operated; in 2024 Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power was engaged to study bringing it into service.
notesEn.VNM: Abandoned the Ninh Thuan nuclear project in 2016; the National Assembly approved reviving it in November 2024.
notesEn.HKG: Buys electricity from the Daya Bay nuclear plant in Guangdong.
notesEn.TWN: Taiwan has had no operating nuclear units since Maanshan unit 2 shut down on 17 May 2025 (Jinshan closed in 2019 and Kuosheng in 2023), so it is classed as phased out. A referendum on 23 August 2025 to restart Maanshan won 74.2% of valid votes, but the yes votes were only 21.7% of eligible voters, short of the 25% threshold. In March 2026 President Lai Ching-te announced plans to restart Maanshan and Kuosheng; Taipower submitted a restart plan for Maanshan to the Nuclear Safety Commission on 27 March (aiming for 2028, and 2029 for Kuosheng). On 31 August 2026 the commission said Taipower had filed a revised plan after the final review meeting; once approved, the plant still needs its own safety inspections and a renewed operating licence. A national referendum on abolishing the nuclear-free homeland policy (Case 22) is set for 28 November 2026.
